message.content:
It looks like there’s a mix‑up in the numbers!  
Boston isn’t typically anywhere near **54 °C**—that would be over 130 °F, hotter than most tropical storms. In reality:

| Season | Typical Highs |
|--------|---------------|
| Summer (June–August) | ~82 °F / 28 °C on warm days, usually ranging from mid‑70s to low‑80s °F (24–29 °C) |
| Winter | Often below freezing, sometimes dipping into the teens Fahrenheit (-10 °C) |

So while Boston does have its share of humid, muggy July afternoons, it rarely reaches temperatures above 90 °F (32 °C), let alone 50+ °C. If you’re planning a trip or just curious about local heat waves, keep an eye on the daily forecasts—they’ll show typical highs in the upper 70s/low 80s rather than anything approaching “hot” in Celsius terms.
